title: No Decisions Without aj
eyebrow: Design proposal · house-rules design loop · nothing built yet
approval: Design approved: no decisions without aj

short.lead: You asked why the plugin lets me settle an unclear point myself and carry on. I read the design loop's code and rules and found three holes. First, once a build starts, every code edit is open, and a question found mid-build has no way back to you. Second, the end-of-reply page check only reports, and it only spots replies that ask a question, so a reply saying "I went with X" passes. Third, the rule text itself allows "routine judgement calls", and helpers hand their questions to the main session, which can answer them itself. The fix adds a Held move that locks code and sends a question page to you, a check that blocks replies which settle something you never chose, and removes the loopholes from the rule text.

changes: new
Held: a way back to aj from inside a build
When a build hits a question, code locks until aj answers on a page.

Today the code lock in _loop_gate (house_rules/design_loop.py:1024) lets every edit through in the Build stage, as long as the issue labels are right. The only moves back are aj's own "QA failed" or a new "Design approved". So when something unclear turns up halfway through a build, nothing stops me from picking an answer and carrying on. The fix adds a Held state. Building a page that has a Choices section while the loop is in Build sets Held. While Held, code edits are refused with a message that names the question page. Held lifts only when aj's own message says "Design approved: <feature>" for the same feature. That approval answers the questions and is logged in docs/6-decisions/Decisions.md like any other approval.
_loop_gate opens every code edit in Build (design_loop.py:1024). There is no move from Build back to aj except QA failed.
A Held flag in the loop file, set by make_page.py when it builds a page with choices during Build, and cleared only by aj's Design approved for that feature.
A mid-build question stops the build. You see a question page, not a finished build with my choice inside it.
new
A check that blocks a reply which decides for aj
A reply that settles a design point you never chose is sent back.

The end-of-reply check only looks for replies that offer choices: _offers_choices (design_loop.py:1712) needs the reply to end with a question mark (line 1717). A reply that says "I chose", "I went with", "I assumed", "I defaulted to" or "for now I'll" ends in a full stop, so it is never seen. A new checkpoint row, decided for aj, looks for that wording in my reply and in each helper's hand-back report. When it finds it, the reply is blocked until it either links a page that puts the point to aj as a choice, or quotes aj's own message that already settled it. The word list is a starting value: it catches the usual phrasings and will miss some, and QA measures how many.
CHECKPOINTS (design_loop.py:1911) has no row that looks for decisions; the page row only reacts to questions.
A blocking decided-for-aj row, run on my reply and on helper reports.
A choice I made without you is caught before you read the reply, not found later in the code.
chg
The page check blocks again for choices and decisions
Long replies stay report-only; replies that offer or make a choice block.
Since plugin 2.68.1 (#309) the page row is report-only (design_loop.py:1914), although the injected rules still say a missing page keeps blocking. The rules and the code disagree.
A reply that offers a choice or trips the decided-for-aj row is blocked until it links a page, with the existing three-block limit. A reply that is only long stays report-only, as #309 chose.
#309 downgraded the row because it blocked sessions too often. Splitting it keeps that relief for long replies while restoring the block where a decision is at stake.
chg
The loopholes come out of the rule text
No exception for routine judgement calls; helpers' questions go to aj.

rules/show-dont-tell.md:12 and rules/detail/clear-writing.md:61 say routine judgement calls go to aj "unless they have said otherwise". The helper start-up note (design_loop.py:970) sends anything unexpected "back to the main session", and agents/builder.md:11 says "stop and ask" without saying whom.

The exception is removed (see the choice below). The helper note and builder.md say an unclear point is reported as a question for aj, never answered by the main session or the helper. The main session puts it on a question page, which sets Held.
The rule text is the only part the model reads directly, so a written exception is a standing invitation to use it.
choices: What should happen to the "unless they have said otherwise" exception for judgement calls?
Every unclear point goes to you, with no exception. This matches "ever, period".
Keep it, but only from a recorded file
You list the kinds of call I may make in docs/page-style.json or a new file. Nothing outside the list counts, and nothing said in chat counts.
You said ever, period. A written exception is exactly what the model leans on, so the clean fix is to remove it.
What should the decided-for-aj check do when it finds decision wording?
Block until a page links, up to three times
The same strength as the restored page block. After three blocks in a row it lets the reply through with a note, so a broken builder cannot loop a session.
Strictest, but a false match on harmless wording can stall a session with nobody watching.
It names the decision in a note but does not stop the reply. This is the strength that failed you today.
Three blocks is the limit you already chose for the page rule (#283), and it keeps a false match from looping a session.
Your "Design approved: <feature>" for the same feature
It reuses the approval you already type, and the decisions log entry rule applies.
Clearer in the log, but one more phrase to remember.
Easiest, but a reply that does not answer the question would lift the lock.
Reusing Design approved keeps one phrase for every design decision and needs no new parsing.

wrapup.summary: The plugin lets me decide for you because a build has no way back to you, the end-of-reply check only notices questions and only reports, and the rule text allows judgement calls. The fix closes all three.
